extracted.intended_audience: university administrators, instructional designers, quality-assurance professionals, and online learning practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for assuring quality and making financial/pricing decisions in online higher-education delivery (covers costing/TDABC and jurisdictional QA frameworks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a realistic allocation base
rubrics_metrics.description: Select an allocation base that reflects realistic, not ideal, activity levels (e.g., staff actual hours worked will be less than theoretical maximums).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: instead of 1,920 hrs/yr use ~80% (1,536 hrs). Use realistic assumptions about sickness, breaks, training, etc., when estimating hours or other bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate an appropriate hourly rate for each cost type
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert salaries and other recurring costs into hourly (or per-unit) application rates using the chosen realistic allocation base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: programmer's $60,000 salary / 1,536 hrs = $39/hr. Apply same approach to other personnel and cost types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create indirect cost pools and application rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Group indirect costs into pools (e.g., Administration, Building, Liability Insurance) and determine an appropriate allocation base and application rate for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Administration allocated on manager hours; Building allocated on project-days; Insurance allocated per project. Compute application rates (e.g., $2/day building, $50/project insurance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine direct and indirect rates to estimate project price
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the calculated hourly/application rates together with time/day estimates to produce a quoted price for a project or course offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example calculation shown: programmer time + administration + building (days × rate) + insurance = quoted price ($16,070 in example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare quoted (estimated) vs actual costs and compute net result
rubrics_metrics.description: After project completion, compute actual costs using the same allocation rules and compare to quoted revenue to determine profit/loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: quoted revenue $16,070 vs actual costs $16,150 → net loss $80. Use this comparison to identify discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate causes of over- or under-application of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: When allocations differ materially from actuals, identify plausible causes (e.g., salary estimates wrong, hours billed differ, number of projects differs, actual costs exceed estimates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example causes provided for programmer over-application, administration under-application, building under-application, and insurance under-application. Use findings to inform rate adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust application rates and cost pools based on experience
rubrics_metrics.description: If estimates are materially wrong or new fixed costs arise, revise allocation bases, adjust application rates, or create new cost pools for future pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor estimate errors are tolerable; gross errors should be corrected and applied to future quotations. TDABC can provide more accurate information on process costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use time-driven activity-based costing (TDABC) to inform pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply TDABC to obtain more accurate information about the costs and underlying efficiency of value-creating processes for online learning offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TDABC helps allocate costs to activities and can improve pricing decisions as online learning increasingly relies on revenue-generating activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base financial decisions on relevant incremental costs and present value
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers should consider only future cash flows that differ among alternatives and, for multi-period cash flows, discount to present value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investments produce cash flows over time, use present-value techniques (P = F/(1 + r)) and multi-period present-value tables provided in appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear statements of educational goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality educational delivery should include explicit, intelligible statements of learning goals for students, employers, faculty, regulators, and other stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a basic characteristic shared across quality-assurance frameworks examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain institutional commitment to support learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must demonstrate ongoing commitment and resources devoted to supporting learners as part of quality assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment should be visible to students, staff, regulators and the public and be part of institutional quality evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in collaborative processes of discovery to improve teaching and learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality frameworks should encourage collaborative inquiry and continual improvement that contributes to enhancing the teaching–learning environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle emphasizes collegial, scholarly approaches rather than purely bureaucratic compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge that quality is relative to stakeholder expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality is a construct experienced relative to different stakeholders (students, faculty, administrators, employers, accreditors, public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality-assurance activity must foster agreement around common goals because perceptions of quality vary across stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include self-review as a core QA component while recognizing external pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessment and internal review are important QA mechanisms, though many frameworks are driven by external regulatory or market concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective QA balances internal improvement with external accountability; self-review feeds institutional planning and audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious applying TQM/CQI/management-by-measure approaches in academia
rubrics_metrics.description: Management frameworks (TQM, CQI, ISO, Baldridge) emphasize measurement and control, but their corporate language and uniformity assumptions may clash with academic values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement can drive improvement but also control; consider social/academic implications before wholesale adoption. Use benchmarks thoughtfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize outcomes (learning/results) over inputs alone
rubrics_metrics.description: QA systems should address fundamental integrity of the learning environment and measure outcomes, not just inputs (seat time, instructor credentials) or simple outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticisms of existing systems include overemphasis on inputs; better QA links processes to demonstrable learning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: New-paradigm QA measures for online learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes of modern QA measures: learner-centred, local/tailored, open, collaborative, respectful, qualitative, flexible, learning-as-constant (time variable), teacher-skilled, aggregated experience, international/global, dynamic, distributed-delivery, outcomes- and service-oriented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These contrast with older, institution-centred measures and are suggested as more appropriate for online/blended contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old-paradigm QA measures (limitations to avoid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional measures are characterized as teacher/institution-centred, centralized, one-size-fits-all, quantitative, prescriptive, time-as-constant (seat-time), teacher-credentialed, static, single-delivery-mode, inputs/process/infrastructure-focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize these limitations when adapting QA to online contexts; avoid uncritical transplantation of seat-time and other input metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize asynchronous interactive learning as a signature characteristic
rubrics_metrics.description: Asynchronous interactive activities (collaboration, communication, engaging content with group and individual tasks) are a defining feature of many online learning environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality frameworks should assess whether an offering leverages asynchronous interactivity rather than merely replicating classroom lectures online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid simply replicating the classroom; exploit online affordances
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality online instruction should not merely emulate face-to-face delivery but should maximize configurations of knowing and community possible online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should focus on interaction, collaboration, and tasks suited to distributed/online modalities rather than passive lecture delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate QA procedures to qualify for self-accrediting status (jurisdictional requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: In some jurisdictions (example: Australia), institutions must show proactive, rigorous, ongoing planning and self-assessment processes to be self-accrediting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of QA procedures, institutional audits, and outcomes to meet state/territorial or national regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use national qualification frameworks to communicate expected achievement standards
rubrics_metrics.description: National qualification frameworks help articulate expected standards for each level of post-secondary achievement and inform QA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA and program design should align learning outcomes and credential levels with national frameworks to aid comparability and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support international cooperation and quality marks for cross-border delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: International initiatives (e.g., UNESCO/OECD statements, EFQUEL, European Quality Mark proposals) aim to harmonize recognition and reduce abuses in transnational delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-border providers should seek reciprocal recognition, federated marks, or adherence to international statements to increase credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide consumer-focused information and course-level review mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality assurance can include market-facing tools: buyer’s guides, online directories, course reviews, and consumer education to help prospective students assess offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: online directories, course reviews (akin to Amazon-style reviews), ratemyprofessor.com; but leaving market-alone to determine quality is cautioned against as unethical/inefficient.
